production.waterSource: Established specialist sources record process water from local natural spring and field-drain sources, with burn water used for cooling.
production.malt: Malt is sourced commercially; current specialist references describe predominantly unpeated malt for core production.
production.fermentation: Current specialist reporting records nine stainless-steel washbacks of approximately 34,000 litres and a fermentation time of about 55 hours.
production.stills: Macduff operates five copper pot stills in an unusual two-wash/three-spirit configuration. The stills have upward-tilting lyne arms with pronounced right-angle kinks; the spirit stills use horizontal shell-and-tube condensers, helping create a weighty, nutty spirit while the rising lyne arms add reflux.
production.maturation: Macduff spirit destined for single malt and blends is matured within Bacardi/Dewar's warehousing; specialist sources also document on-site/racked and dunnage storage historically.

houseCharacter: Macduff's short fermentation gives the wash a relatively direct, cereal and nutty base rather than an intensely ester-driven one. The unusual five-still configuration, kinked rising lyne arms and cold shell-and-tube condensation balance reflux against a weightier, slightly sulphury new-make character. That combination gives the spirit body and nuttiness while preserving enough fruit to keep it from becoming blunt.
cask23Narrative: Macduff is technically unusual because its stillhouse uses two wash stills and three spirit stills rather than matching pairs. Rising lyne arms and shell-and-tube condensers pull the spirit in two directions at once: some extra reflux and fruit, but also enough weight to retain a nutty, robust core. It is a useful distillery for understanding how condenser temperature and lyne-arm geometry can matter as much as still shape itself.
